title: Sparks of Rationality: Do Reasoning LLMs Align with Human Judgment and Choice?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM responses on canonical behavioral economics tasks (e.g., risk seeking, ambiguity aversion, loss aversion, temporal discounting, and the endowment effect) to test compliance with rational choice axioms and expected utility theory.

Using in-context priming (ICP) and representation-level steering (RLS) to induce specific affective states (e.g., fear, anger, sadness, disgust) and measuring how these emotions systematically shift model behavior in risk evaluation, moral condemnation, legal blame, and prosocial choices.
